claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to gather some information about you and your children.

Let me start with the first question:

**How many children are you inquiring about for Child Benefit, and what are their names?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! I'm inquiring about my child. His name is Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you're inquiring about one child, Alex.

Now, to assess eligibility, I need to gather some details about your situation.

**What is Alex's date of birth?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's 8 years old. He was born in March 2017.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you! So Alex was born in March 2017, making him 8 years old.

**Are you Alex's parent or guardian, and do you have responsibility for him?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I'm his parent and I have responsibility for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that. I need to understand your living situation with Alex.

**Does Alex live with you in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives with me here in the UK. We live in Manchester.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good, thank you. Now I need to gather some information about your residency and work situation.

**Are you a UK citizen, or what is your residency status in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm a UK citizen, yes.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that. Now I have a question about your work situation.

**Are you currently working, and if so, are you working in the UK or abroad?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm currently working here in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I have just a couple more questions to complete my assessment.

**What is your current annual income, or approximately how much do you earn per year?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'd rather not say exactly, but I do work. Why do you need to know my income? I thought Child Benefit was available to everyone?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's a fair question! You're right that Child Benefit is quite widely available. Let me clarify: Child Benefit itself doesn't have an income limit for eligibility. However, there is a separate tax charge called the "High Income Child Benefit Charge" that applies if your income exceeds a certain threshold. This charge doesn't make you ineligible for Child Benefit, but it does affect how much you keep.

Since you'd prefer not to share your exact income, that's completely fine – it won't prevent me from assessing your basic eligibility for Child Benefit.

Let me ask one more important question:

**Have you claimed Child Benefit for Alex before, or is this a new claim?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: This is a new claim. I've never claimed Child Benefit for Alex before.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent, thank you for that information. I have just one final question to complete my assessment.

**Are there any other children living with you that you haven't mentioned, or is Alex your only child?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex is my only child.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect, thank you for answering all my questions. I now have enough information to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit.

Let me review your situation:
- You are the parent and have responsibility for Alex
- Alex is 8 years old (born March 2017)
- Alex lives with you in the UK (Manchester)
- You are a UK citizen
- You are working in the UK
- This is a new claim for Alex

Based on the Child Benefit eligibility rules, you meet all the key requirements for Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Congratulations! **You are eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.**

You meet all the criteria needed to claim Child Benefit. Alex is under 16 years old, lives with you in the UK, and you have parental responsibility for him as a UK citizen and resident.

You can proceed with submitting a new claim for Child Benefit for Alex. If you have any other questions about your eligibility, I'm happy to help!
